headline: Bank of Mexico Cuts Interest Rate to 6.25% in Split Vote
summary: In a divided 3-2 vote, Banco de Mexico's governing board surprised markets by lowering the benchmark interest rate to 6.25%.
why: Monetary policy easing by emerging market central banks impacts local bond yields and currency valuations relative to foreign capital flows.

impacts.name: Mexican Peso
impacts.why: Lower interest rates reduce yield differentials supporting the domestic currency, potentially weakening the peso.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: An unexpected interest rate cut by the central bank lowered borrowing costs and shifted yield expectations.
